## Method: stack-based forward parsing

I pushed each opening bracket onto a stack, and on each closing bracket checked that it matched the top. Any mismatch would mean the input is malformed, and any leftover entries are the brackets that still need closing.

**Part 1: `< ( ( [ < > { [ { ( ) } ] < { < { } > [ ( < > ) ] } > } [ < > ] ] )`**

- `< ( ( [` → stack `< ( ( [`
- `< >` balanced; `{ [ { ( ) } ]` balanced → `< ( ( [ {`
- `< { < { } > [ ( < > ) ] } > }` → every pair matches; net effect on stack: `< ( ( [ {` (the `{` closed by the final `}`) → `< ( ( [`
- `[ < > ] ]` → `[` pushed and popped, then second `]` pops the original `[` → `< ( (`
- `)` pops the inner `(` → **`< (`**

**Part 2: `{ { ( { ( ( [ ( [ ] ) ] < { } > ) ) { { ( [ [ ] ] ) } [ ( ) ] { { [ ] } } } } ) } ( { } ) }`**

Starting from `< (`:

- `{ { ( { ( ( [ ( [ ] ) ] < { } > ) )` → `< ( { { ( {`
- `{ { ( [ [ ] ] ) }` → `< ( { { ( { {`
- `[ ( ) ]` balanced → unchanged
- `{ { [ ] } } } }` → after pushing two `{` and popping four closers, the stack is `< ( { { (`
- `)` pops `(` → `< ( { {`
- `}` pops `{` → `< ( {`
- `( { } )` balanced → unchanged
- `}` pops `{` → **`< (`**

The stack never mismatches, so the input is well-formed up to this point. The two unclosed brackets, in order from innermost, are `(` then `<`.

**Completion:** `)` closes `(`, then `>` closes `<`.
